# AUROC per perturbation against the component count K, validation and test
# figure: auroc_per_perturbation_vs_K
# source: /home/paul/Code/Atoms_Carla/data/TFV6/results_alt/<K> clusters/atoms_analysis_mode_2 + the labelled val/test splits
# Generated by figure_notes.py — do not edit; regenerate with the figure.

    Sweep: K = 1 and 2 to 20. K = 1 is the single-Gaussian, no-clustering baseline, built the same way as in auroc_val_test_vs_K.txt.
    A panel is one perturbation's frames against the clean frames only, so a panel is NOT a pool and the four panels do not average to the K-selection curve, which drops Gaussian noise. The mean of the other three panels does.
    Each curve is the unweighted mean over the four GMM detectors, the same averaging step as auroc_val_test_vs_K. k-NN-GMM uses each K's own val-selected k.
    Shared y-axis on purpose: the panels sit at very different heights and that is the finding.
    The same 1000 frames per split are scored at every K, so the points are not independent comparisons.
    No rise/plateau/shape descriptors: K is not a severity knob.

The k-th-NN fallback across the sweep
-------------------------------------
    The clustered k-th-NN entry in the mean uses each K's own val-selected k, while the components shrink as K grows. Once a component holds fewer frames than k, every sample routed to it is scored against the full baseline instead, so the entry changes character across the sweep.
